name: FilterChip
purpose: One filter, on or off, shown next to the results it narrows.
notFor: Exactly one of a set. That is SegmentedControl — a row of independent toggles cannot express 'exactly one', and 'none selected' is legal here and illegal there.
A fact about the row rather than something the reader asked for. That is Badge, which refuses to be clickable for this reason.
More than a handful of values. That is Select.
A chosen value with a way to take it back. That is RemovableChip.

anatomy.note: Also carries bh-chip--filter. The base bh-chip rules are shared with RemovableChip so the two cannot render differently.
The non-colour cue for the pressed state. aria-hidden, and it holds its box when off so pressing a chip does not reflow the row beside it.

label.meaning: The visible text, and the accessible name.
label.note: One string for both, so they cannot differ. A chip whose name is not what it says on it is not a voice-control target (WCAG 2.5.3).

pressed.note: Rendered three ways: aria-pressed, the check mark, and the selection tint. The tint alone would fail WCAG 1.4.1.

keyboard.Tab: Moves focus to the chip. Each chip is its own tab stop — they are independent toggles, not a roving-tabindex group.

aria.labelling: From label, rendered as the button's text content. Required.
aria.focus: Ring from bh-focusable, never removed. A set of chips should sit in a named group (role="group" with aria-label) or they are unrelated buttons with nothing saying what they filter.
aria.announcements: None of its own. aria-pressed carries the state and is announced on focus; the check mark is aria-hidden so it is not announced twice.

attributes.aria-pressed: true when the filter is applied, false when it is not — never absent, because absence means 'not a toggle'
attributes.type: button, fixed rather than defaulted: a filter beside a form must not submit it

content.label: The value being filtered on, as the reader would say it. Not "Filter: Finance" — the group's name says it is a filter.
